findings.description: Hazy, ill-defined opacity in the right lower zone with apparent right basal volume loss, obscuring the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm. It is present on both studies. On the current film the haze appears to reach the lower right mid zone.
findings.evidence: The opacity sits in the same place on both films with the same loss of the right heart border and medial hemidiaphragm. The apparently greater extent on the current film may be explained by the AP projection, underexposure and overlying soft tissue.

findings.description: Right hemidiaphragm contour is elevated and indistinct medially on both studies, with an aerated lateral costophrenic sulcus.
findings.evidence: The high right basal contour is seen on both the PA prior and the AP current. Its apparent height differs with projection and beam angle, so interval change cannot be judged.

findings.description: Cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current. The right heart border is obscured on both.
findings.evidence: The heart shadow looks wider on the current film, but AP projection magnifies the heart. The obscured right border also limits assessment of width on both films.

findings.description: Right hilar and infrahilar prominence, continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies. Vessels, adjacent lung opacity and a hilar lesion cannot be separated on these films.
findings.evidence: Right hilar density is greater than the left on both films. Mild rotation on both, the projection difference and the overlapping lower zone opacity prevent any call on size or change.

findings.description: Prominent aortic knuckle with an unfolded aortic contour on both studies. The upper mediastinum looks wider on the AP current.
findings.evidence: The aortic knuckle has the same shape and position on both films. The apparent mediastinal widening on the current film is expected with AP projection and is not called as a change.

cant_determine.question: Has the right lower zone opacity changed in size or density since the prior?
cant_determine.reason: Prior is PA and current is AP and underexposed. Projection and exposure differences can make a basal opacity look larger or denser.
cant_determine.recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able.

cant_determine.question: Is there a right pleural effusion, including a subpulmonic component, and has it changed?
cant_determine.reason: The high, indistinct right basal contour with an aerated lateral sulcus could reflect subpulmonic fluid, an elevated hemidiaphragm, or basal volume loss. A frontal film alone cannot separate these, and patient position on the current AP is not shown.
cant_determine.recommend: Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest.

cant_determine.reason: The right hilum merges with the adjacent opacity on both films. Mild rotation and the AP projection make hilar size unreliable.
cant_determine.recommend: CT chest, with contrast if appropriate.

cant_determine.question: Has heart size changed?
cant_determine.reason: AP projection magnifies the heart, and cardiothoracic ratio is valid on PA films only. The right heart border is also obscured on both studies.
cant_determine.recommend: Repeat PA film when the patient is able, or echocardiography if clinically relevant.

cant_determine.reason: The true diaphragm is not separately visible on a frontal film. The lordotic AP beam angle on the current film also alters the apparent dome height.
cant_determine.recommend: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant and right base, or CT covering the chest and upper abdomen.

cant_determine.reason: The current film is underexposed with heavy soft tissue overlap, and the clavicles project over the apices. Small nodules cannot be confirmed or excluded.
cant_determine.recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral with adequate exposure.

response.limits: This is a blind first read of two single frontal radiographs, with no lateral views, no indication and no dates. The prior is PA and the current is AP and underexposed, so no size change is reported for any finding. No measurements are given because the images carry no pixel scale and magnification is unknown. The images are downsampled, so fine detail such as margins, calcification, cavitation and subtle rib lesions should be reviewed on the source images in PACS. Patient identity match is assumed from the similar aortic contour and right basal abnormality and has not been verified. This is a draft for resident and attending review.
